title: EXAHD GENE Run on Hazel Hen Supercomputer
author: Theresa Pollinger
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.u63ezgn

steps.title: Define scenario and open issue
steps.instruction: Create one or more related scenarios, save each as a parameters file (or ctparam file for combigrid runs) and upload it to https://simsgs.informatik.uni-stuttgart.de:8444/EXAHD/ParameterFiles. Then open an issue on https://simsgs.informatik.uni-stuttgart.de:8444/EXAHD/ParameterFiles/boards so collaborators can review it. After the issue is created, add label 1.

substeps.instruction: Define scenario(s) and create parameter (or ctparam) file(s)
Push the file(s) to the ParameterFiles repository
Create an issue on the project board
Add label 1 to the issue

steps.title: Log into Hazel Hen and sync files
steps.instruction: Open an SSH session with reverse port forwarding using `ssh -R 7890:simsgs.informatik.uni-stuttgart.de:22 ipvuser@hazelhen.hww.de`. Inside the session, run `git pull /lustre/cray/ws8/ws/ipvpolli-EXAHD/ParameterFiles` to update the ParameterFiles repository.

substeps.instruction: Run `ssh -R 7890:simsgs.informatik.uni-stuttgart.de:22 ipvuser@hazelhen.hww.de`
Execute `git pull /lustre/cray/ws8/ws/ipvpolli-EXAHD/ParameterFiles`

steps.title: Create new problem directory
steps.instruction: Navigate to `/lustre/cray/ws8/ws/ipvpolli-EXAHD/gene-dev/` and execute `./newprob`, which creates a new problem directory named `prob<number>` (replace `<number>` with the generated identifier). Inside that directory, place a symlink or copy of the desired parameters file and name it `parameters`. Verify that the output folder named `diagdir` referenced in the parameters file already exists.

substeps.instruction: Run `./newprob` in `/lustre/cray/ws8/ws/ipvpolli-EXAHD/gene-dev/`
Symlink or copy the chosen parameters file to `prob<number>/parameters`
Ensure the `diagdir` folder specified in the parameters file exists

steps.title: Prepare and commit submission script
steps.instruction: Download the template submit script from https://gitlab.mpcdf.mpg.de/ext-ec8a21db5900/gene-dev/blob/exahd/makefiles/hazel_hen/qsub_hazel_hen.sh and place it in the problem directory. Edit the script to set the required number of cores and wall‑time for your run. If you have modified the GENE installation or the parameters file, commit those changes now, referencing the issue URL in the commit message. After committing, add label 2 to the issue.

substeps.instruction: Retrieve the template script from the given URL
Copy it into the `prob<number>` directory
Edit the script to specify cores and wall‑time
Commit any changes to the installation or parameters file, mentioning the issue link
Add label 2 to the issue

steps.title: Archive problem directory with git‑annex
steps.instruction: git‑annex stores metadata in the ParameterFiles repository while the actual files reside elsewhere; therefore copy or move the entire `prob<number>` directory to a sensible location under `/lustre/cray/ws8/ws/ipvpolli-EXAHD/ParameterFiles`. In the commit message, include the commit hashes of the GENE version used, the combigrid module (if applicable), and the parameters file. Then add label 4 to the issue.

substeps.instruction: Copy or move `prob<number>` to `/lustre/cray/ws8/ws/ipvpolli-EXAHD/ParameterFiles`
Commit the move with a message that lists the GENE version hash, combigrid module hash (if any), and parameters file hash
Add label 4 to the issue

steps.title: Decide post‑run analysis location
steps.instruction: Based on the scientific goal, choose whether to (a) transfer the output files to the Draco system for GENE diagnostics, (b) pull them to your local workstation for visualization, or (c) perform the heavy computation directly on Hazel Hen. Record the chosen option in the issue and add label 5.

substeps.instruction: Select the desired post‑run analysis platform
Document the choice in the issue
Add label 5 to the issue

steps.title: Submit job and monitor
steps.instruction: From the problem directory, run `qsub /lustre/cray/ws8/ws/ipvpolli-EXAHD/gene-dev/prob<number>/qsub_hazel_hen.sh` to submit the job to the scheduler. After submission, add label 3 to the issue and wait for the job to finish.

substeps.instruction: Execute the qsub command with the correct path
Add label 3 to the issue
Monitor the job until completion
